extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: practicing scientists and educated general readers (early 20th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Short reviews, letters, and notes for a scientific weekly (Nature) evaluating books, ships, geological reports, and institutional practice; mixes critical appraisal and reporting for a learned readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of Mendelism's general applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: If Mendelism deals with any other problem but that of sex, what is that problem? If no other problem can be named, what is the evidence that Mendelism deals with anything more than those abnormalities of sexual reproduction which occur under conditions of artificial selection?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand indication that Mendelian principles have conceivable bearing on heredity in general rather than only on curiosities of artificial breeding; avoid assuming laboratory ‘precision’ reproduces natural conditions without factual support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of survivals of ancient customs in archaeological interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of ancient customs (e.g., 'kern-baby'/corn-baby, Beltane fires, youths jumping through fire) is of great importance when trying to ascertain functions of stone circles and cromlechs because early missionaries adapted many pagan festivals to Christian worship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect contemporary survivals of festival customs, especially in promising fields (Wales), and report unrecorded practices to illuminate interpretation of megalithic structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-impression and detail evaluation of large ship design
rubrics_metrics.description: The first impression of the Mauretania is one of colossal size; the last is wondering amazement at the forethought and design which appear in details, trivial in themselves, but of supreme importance to individual comfort, of the fittings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both overall scale and small design details because minor fittings can have outsized impact on passenger comfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maneuverability in constrained waterways
rubrics_metrics.description: In narrow winding rivers (the Tyne) the handiness of the vessel was immediately apparent: proceeding under her own steam, steered by propellers and the rudder, she was easily manoeuvred at the sharp bends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ship handling in real constrained conditions (rivers, crowded waterways) to judge maneuverability rather than relying on open-sea trials alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of turbine control responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: It was obvious that the great turbines, which in the aggregate can develop 70,000 h.p., can be stopped or started with ease and certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test start/stop responsiveness and fine control of large turbine systems as a key operational criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterisation and mapping of vibration in turbine-propelled ships
rubrics_metrics.description: Vibration is noticeable though relatively slight; generally maximal in the after part and diminishes thence to the bows, but distribution is erratic with regions of maximal vibration close to regions of minimal vibration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record spatial distribution and periodicity of vibration aboard turbine ships; look for periodic crescendo–climax–quiet patterns suggesting synchronism between propellers and investigate by altering screw RPMs; use pallograph to register shaft movements and vibrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis testing for causes of vibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Vibration has been referred to impact of water thrown by wing propellers against ship sides, unequal thrusts of blades, and twisting couples when propellers synchronise; inequalities arise from skin friction dragging water near the side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider multiple mechanical hydrodynamic mechanisms; test synchronism effects (e.g., offsetting screw RPMs) to reduce vibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumentation for measuring turbine work (torsion meters)
rubrics_metrics.description: As it is not possible to get an indicator diagram of a turbine, the work done is measured on the Mauretania by torsion meters directly applied to each shaft: two wheels on the shaft provide electrical contacts whose lag measures torsion; calibrated by shop determinations of twist under known couples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use torsion meters calibrated in controlled conditions; mounting dials/indicators on the bridge can provide moment-to-moment display of each turbine's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engine-room control ergonomics
rubrics_metrics.description: The controlling platform of the engine-room is impressive where a few small levers control the gigantic forces of the turbines; the small wheel in the wheel-house, by means of a small hydraulic motor, controls the enormous steering-engine sunk below water level some 650 feet distant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess simplicity and ease of operation of controls (minimal levers, efficient hydraulic steering linkage) given the scale of power being managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material selection for weight savings and corrosion concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Plates were delivered rolled to a guaranteed thickness saving 500 tons dead weight; use of silicon steel in boilers saved 500 tons; aluminium used in decorative lifts saved 20 tons but raises question whether high affinity for chlorine and sea-air chlorides have been adequately taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance dead-weight savings from novel materials against long-term corrosion/performance concerns in marine environment; document guaranteed tolerances and expected service effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engine-room spatial arrangement and ventilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite absence of main reciprocating engines, the engine-room is closely packed; steam pipes arch large enough for a boy to walk through; exhaust from low-pressure turbine passes through a 14 ft by 16 ft pipe; stokeholds are efficiently ventilated by powerful fans and are cool save when furnace doors are opened despite 192 furnaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate spatial layout for maintenance access, routing of large exhausts, and effectiveness of ventilation systems in stokeholds under heavy firing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural provision for longitudinal flexing (bellying)
rubrics_metrics.description: The magnitude of the strains in a ship nearly the length of the Houses of Parliament must experience in heavy head seas is provided for by cutting the boat deck and deck house completely through in three places to allow the ship to give longitudinally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design intentional longitudinal cuts/joints or other measures to permit controlled flexing and avoid structural damage in heavy seas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of pioneer and unofficial fieldwork in geology
rubrics_metrics.description: Pioneer work, though unofficial, is not to be contemned since it is often done under conditions of considerable difficulty by enthusiastic geologists whose labours have laid the foundation for detailed work of Government surveyors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise and integrate high-quality private or pioneer surveys into broader mapping efforts; they can provide crucial initial data in difficult areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stratigraphic division by lithology and local variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Griquatown Series divided into upper group (slaty rocks, jasperoid, chert, limestone), middle group (Ongeluk volcanic beds, banded jasper), lower group (banded jaspers, quartzites, mudstones); volcanic series up to ~5000 feet; local variations (acid/intermediate lavas, tuffs, agglomerates) must be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lithologic criteria to subdivide series; record thicknesses, interbedded volcanic/sedimentary units and local lithofacies for accurate regional correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of striated and flattened pebbles as glacial evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Conglomeratic rocks near top of lower group contain 'striated and flattened pebbles and boulders' which, according to Mr. Rogers, 'certainly owe their characteristic shape and scratches to glacial action'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such clast morphology and striations occur, consider glacial processes even if strata are much older than other known glacial formations; discuss implications for paleoglaciation history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping formations and naming conventions with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Three series — Black Reef, Campbell Rand, and Griquatown — are grouped as the Transvaal System (a term introduced by Molengraaff); the name is scarcely a happy one but adopted by Transvaal Geological Survey so will probably remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about regional nomenclature and equivalence; note when names are adopted by official surveys even if imperfect and explain correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and reporting of unconformities and basement relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ventersdorp, Transvaal, and Matsap systems lie on a floor of granite and schists and have been folded; there exist unconformities between certain series (e.g., Zoetvlei Beds and overlying units) and granite–schist relationships vary regionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document unconformities, folding events, and basement relationships clearly; these are key to regional geological history and correlation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation of Karroo (Karoo) rocks across regions using lithology and fossil finds
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey concludes Bushveld Sandstone Series and overlying amygdaloids are equivalent to Red Beds, Cave Sandstone, and Volcanic Group of Stormberg Series; discovery of fossil bones of Stormberg age in Zoutpansberg shows Bushveld unit extended far north.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lithologic similarity and fossil evidence (when present) to correlate formations across wide areas; new fossil finds can extend known extents of units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular-science treatment: demystify by showing development
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of the writer of such a volume is largely to rob his subject of its atmosphere of romance by showing its gradual development and the reasonableness of its results; the author treats it in an easy manner and illustrates it well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For popular scientific books assume little prior knowledge, emphasize historical development and explanations rather than pure marveling, and use illustrations each with definite reason for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance breadth with accuracy in comprehensive popular works
rubrics_metrics.description: When many branches of the subject are dealt with one expects to discover a few inaccuracies; slips of this kind are not very serious and are very few.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for factual accuracy but recognise that broad surveys may contain minor inaccuracies; flag and correct clear technical overstatements (e.g., incorrect shutter exposure times or misstatements about viewing Lippmann photographs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership criteria for national observatory directors
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors do not enjoy unfettered discretion; large pieces of work requiring ample time and funds must be supervised; a director should support and, if possible, bring to conclusion long legacy projects like star catalogues and international charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutional leaders on capacity to steward long-term major projects, provide encouragement and organisation for international schemes, and complete legacy tasks to relieve institutional burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designing astronomical instruments for stability and error control
rubrics_metrics.description: The equatorial coudé was designed to obtain greater stability than ordinary equatorials and by taking advantage of this stability to measure large angular distances; determining sources of error inherent in the instrument is essential before using it for new precise methods (e.g., measuring constant of aberration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to adopting novel observational methods, analyse instrument error sources, design for mechanical stability, and use clever measurement schemes (double mirror, selecting stars of same altitude, measuring six months apart) to amplify target quantities and minimize refraction effects.
